hints.title: Add the missing graph with exact landmarks
hints.body: Draw y=tanx through (0,0) and (±π/4,±1), increasing between its vertical asymptotes at x=±π/2. Keep the two supplied graphs in place.
hints.recap: Comparisons must use the three heights at the same input x.
hints.pitfall: The supplied curves have input 2x; the added tangent has input x.
hints.pause: Mark the tangent at −π/4, 0 and π/4 on the given axes.

recall.reminder: Use standard values and input scales to sketch a trigonometric graph.

hints.title: Track possible orders between crossings
hints.body: Inspect intervals on either side of the labelled quarter-turn points and near the ends of the domain, recording all three function heights at a common x.
hints.recap: A crossing can change the ordering.
hints.pitfall: Strict inequalities cannot use the crossing itself as a witness.
hints.pause: Find witnesses for as many proposed orders as possible.

recall.reminder: A crossing can change the ordering.

hints.title: Test the missing ordering globally
hints.body: If an ordering requires tangent above both supplied curves, determine every interval where that is possible, then examine the sine-cosine order within those intervals.
hints.recap: One necessary part of an ordering can conflict with another.
hints.pitfall: Failure at one test input does not establish impossibility everywhere.
hints.pause: Prove which proposed ordering has no witness.

recall.reminder: One necessary part of an ordering can conflict with another.

solution:
Overlay the increasing tangent curve using its zeros, asymptotes and values tan(±π/4)=±1.

The sketch gives examples of A just above π/4, B just below π/4, D just above −π/4, E just below −π/4, and F close to −π/2.

For tangent to exceed both other functions requires π/4<x<π/2. There, cos2x<0<sin2x, which rules out the order sin2x<cos2x<tanx. C is the statement that is not true.
